devices.modulation_format: PAM-4 at 120-180 GBd and PAM-8 at 120-160 GBd, NGMI vs symbol rate; PAM-8 140 GBd error-free under SC-LDPC (5/6) plus BCH (0.9915) FEC; PAM-4 180 GBd NGMI above threshold 0.8714
devices.notes: Only the I channel of the I/Q chip is characterized. Vpi 3.26 V is the modulator's own measurement, taken stand-alone in GSG fashion (implied; drive not stated explicitly), so entered as push-pull MZM Vpi; it was not measured under the differential driver. Authors' Vpi*L 1.1 V cm is referenced to the single-ended signal under differential push-pull drive; it is not reproducible from 3.26 V and 7.5 mm (2.45 V cm; 1.22 V cm if halved), so not entered, and the view derives 2.45 V cm. Stand-alone EO response (Fig. 1(b)) measured to 67 GHz (equipment limit), no 3 dB crossing; S21 normalized to its peak near 5 GHz, noise dips reach about -3 dB near 60 GHz (Fig. 1(b), approx.); EM simulation dashed in the same plot not used. Assembly (driver plus MZM, Fig. 1(d)): 3 dB bandwidth about 60 GHz at mid-gain, wire-bond penalty; terminations 35 ohm instead of 50 ohm. 50 ohm TWE impedance is a design statement (z0_ohm empty). Driver swing 2.8 V per output pair is simulated, not entered. Net 347 Gb/s is 140 GBd PAM-8 under the SC-LDPC plus BCH FEC (rate 0.8262, NGMI threshold 0.8714); 1.4 pJ/bit is the assembly energy on the gross rate, equal to driver IC power (605 mW per channel / 420 Gb/s). PAM-4 at 180 GBd NGMI about 0.95 (Fig. 2(b)), above threshold. Coupling loss above 15 dB (estimated), so 23 dBm into the assembly. Electrode gap, metal, rib geometry, IL not reported.

devices.il_onchip_includes: carrier-induced excess loss at pi (0.20 dB) plus two Si-to-hybrid tapers (0.18 dB each)
devices.notes: Numbers from arXiv v1 (2609.24611v1, 10 pages, 21 Sep 2026); Supplementary Sections I-IX are not in the cached source. Phase-shifting mechanism is carrier accumulation and depletion (plasma dispersion, band filling, Franz-Keldysh) in n-InGaAsP, not Pockels; eo_material=other. VpiL 0.13 V*cm measured on 500 and 1000 um phase shifters (Fig. 2(d)); Vpi 2.2 V is quoted for 600 um without stating how it was obtained (not described as a measurement); consistent with 0.13 V*cm / 0.6 mm = 2.17 V. p.5 also gives 2.3 V as approximately Vpi for 600 um. Wavelength 1550 nm. Fig. 2(e) MZI with 1.1 mm phase shifter shows more than 2 pi tuning (gate -1 to 5 V). Dynamic: 10-90% rise 555 ps and fall 417 ps, 9.375 MHz square wave, 2.0 Vpp on 3.0 V bias (Fig. 2(f)), device length not stated; RC-limited; no S21 bandwidth reported. Static power 28.9 fW/pi (13.3 fA leakage, 600 um); circuit median 21.8 fW; switching energy 15.3 pJ/pi (C = 6.48 pF); not mapped to energy_per_bit_fj (per pi, not per bit). Carrier-induced excess loss 0.20 dB/pi; taper loss 0.18 dB each; il_onchip_db is the section total at pi, loss reference and normalization defined in Supplementary Sections IV-V (not read). Circuit: 4x4 Clements mesh, channel crosstalk below -12 dB, 50 random unitaries R2 0.93, negligible thermal crosstalk. MZI internal and external phase-shifter pairs operated push-pull in the circuit. Phase-shifter drive mode, ER and rib width not reported.

devices.notes: Headline device: 70 unit cells per side, 3.5 um electrode gap (Fig. 3(f),(g); text p.5), 64 um electrode length (Fig. 3(b) dimension; photonic crystal 2 x 70 x 454 nm = 63.6 um; footprint 57.6 um^2 = 64 um x 0.9 um). Resonance near 1568 nm read from Fig. 3(e),(f) (L band; the design resonance is near 1559 nm, Fig. 1(i), shifted by process variation, p.4). Tuning efficiency 24.33 pm/V (Fig. 3(g), Fig. S2(b)); on the reversed voltage axis of Fig. 3(g) (+30 V to -30 V) the resonance blue-shifts for positive voltage (-0.8 nm at +30 V, +0.7 nm at -30 V; Fig. 3(f): the +30 V peak lies at shorter wavelength), so the signed value is -24.33 pm/V (the text and the figure label quote the magnitude; signed-value convention as for the other Pockels resonators in the database). Q 2200 (p.2, 'a Q factor of 2200', type and unit-cell number not stated at that sentence; Fig. 3(d) gives Q 1118 to 3848 for N = 50 to 90). Bandwidth: the small-signal EO S21 (Fig. 3(h)) was measured with a 110 GHz lightwave component analyzer at detunings 0.85 to 1.25 nm; it peaks at about +7 to +9 dB near 60-100 GHz and stays above the -3 dB line to 110 GHz, so >110 GHz with the measurement limit 110 GHz; the gap of the device used for Fig. 3(h) is not stated (assigned here by judgment, as the headline device). The calculated bandwidth above 200 GHz (Eq. 5, perturbation model) is simulated and not entered. IL about 13.7 dB is the N70, 3.5 um point of Fig. S1(a) (peak transmission); the paper does not define what it includes (grating couplers); Fig. 3(e) shows about -14 dB for the same device, Fig. 3(d) spectra are normalized to about 0 dB outside the stop band, so the figures differ in normalization. Energy 0.2 fJ/bit is the authors' C Vpp^2/4 for NRZ (p.6); the capacitance behind it is not stated (the Fig. 2(d) simulated capacitance is near 0 fF on the plotted scale for 50-80 um electrodes) and the scope is modulator CV^2 only. Drive 3 Vpp is the amplifier output stated in the Experimental Section; cable and probe loss not stated. max_baud 220 GBd is the 220 Gb/s NRZ eye (derived); BER measured only to 100 Gb/s NRZ (limited AWG). Not reported: ER, Vpi, optical input power, temperature.

The authors attribute the cut-off to the photon lifetime (32 GHz predicted for Q about 6000, supplement p.17), but it coincides with the stated 30 GHz setup limit (Methods p.6: electrical losses of the probe station and the 26 GHz photodiode make measurements beyond 30 GHz impossible), hence bw_measured_to_ghz = 30; the steepness of the roll-off suggests a setup limit (curator reading, not the authors'). Resonator loss 23 dB/cm is much higher than the 2.9 dB/cm access waveguide because of the 2.3 um electrode gap, chosen to give Q for more than 30 GHz bandwidth. Drive amplitude 1.7 Vpp is estimated from amplifier gain 23 dB and probe-station loss 13 dB (Fig. S10), not measured at the chip; eye opening limited by ASE noise from the optical amplifier (Fig. 4d caption). Energy 45 fJ/bit = 1/4 C V^2 with C = 62 fF (an estimate). No Vpi, VpiL or on-chip IL is entered for this device. The supplement's off-resonance loss is self-contradictory (supplement p.8): with alpha = t = 0.92 (supplement p.7), (alpha+t)^2/(1+alpha t)^2 = 0.993, which is -0.03 dB, but the paper prints '= 0.993 = -0.3 dB'; both readings are kept here and il_onchip_db is left empty. Racetrack electrode length not stated.

devices.notes: Numbers from arXiv v2 (2112.10926v2, 14 pages incl. Supplementary Information); associated journal Nanophotonics 11(17), 4001-4009 (2022). Simulation and design study only (FEM eigenmode, COMSOL RC extraction, 3D FDTD/Lumerical): the only measurement is ellipsometry of the ITO film (Fig. 2(a)); no fabricated or characterized modulator. Table I marks ER, IL, speed and energy of this work as calculated. Mechanism: ITO carrier accumulation/depletion in a MOS capacitor with plasmonic enhancement from the Au top plate (not Pockels); drive +/-3.5 V (7 V swing), carrier density 1.6e20 to 2.5e20 cm-3 in 10 nm ITO. Asymmetric Y-splitter in front of the active arm, 41:59 (X = 41). Fabricating fab not named. Alternative design point of the same stack with splitting ratio X = 91 (91:9): 9.1 um length, ER 53 dB, IL 10 dB, transmission difference 10%, speed 71 GHz (Fig. 4 caption p.7; text p.7). Shown by the authors to illustrate the ER versus IL trade-off; not the headline device. VpiL, capacitance and energy not given for this design.

devices.notes: Device A (Np 20, Nr 10). Vpi 78 V and VpiL 0.96 V cm come from a sinusoidal fit to a transmission change of only about 10 percent over 0-5 V (Fig. S4); the authors state the response is strongly nonlinear (efficiency factor 0.013 pi/V, phase proportional to sqrt(V+Vbi)), so the Vpi is an extrapolation and its convention is not stated. The text says the 10 percent change corresponds to 0.1 pi, but 78 V corresponds to about 0.064 pi over 5 V (source inconsistency); the authors also give alpha*VpiL 286.1 dB V (supplement p.8). Bandwidth: 110 GHz is the crossing of the authors' fit to the S21 trace at 3.5 V bias; the measured trace spans 0 to 110 GHz (Fig. 4(D)); at 4 V the response is said to exceed 110 GHz (row han2023-c; Fig. S11: measured trace to 110 GHz stays above -3 dB, fit about -2.7 dB at the 120 GHz plot edge, no crossing shown, figure read). Rows han2023-a and han2023-c are operating points of one physical device (han2023-device-a). IL: 6.8 dB with 5.4 dB attributed to the phase shifter in the main text (p.5) versus 3.7 dB (29.8 dB/mm x 124 um) implied by supplement Sec. S5. Design-stage simulated values not entered: efficiency factor 0.013 pi/V, optical bandwidth about 140 GHz, electrical bandwidth about 200 GHz at 4 V, Qpropagating about 5000; the authors' microwave group index estimate about 2.1 at 110 GHz is entered as n_rf (supplement Sec. S4). Capacitance 18.6 fF is derived from the authors' model (simulated) junction capacitance 1.5 pF/cm at 3.5 V, per arm (the factor 2 in their Eb formula). Not reported: optical input power, temperature of the headline data, bias for Vpi, Z0, RF loss in dB/cm, operating wavelength of the S21 trace.

band.note: Spectra at 1290-1330 nm; O-band laser (EXFO T200S-O).

il_onchip_db.note: Average off-resonance loss of one MRM, from comparing the MRM spectrum with a grating-coupler pair.

length_mm.note: Doped-region length 40 um used as L in the Vpi*L formula; ring radius 8 um.

max_line_rate_gbps.note: 140 GBd PAM4 eye at 0.73 Vpp, TDECQ 4.85 dB; 16-tap FFE.

rib_width_nm.note: 420 nm wide, 220 nm thick rib.

slab_thickness_nm.note: 70 nm slab; connected to a 220 nm slab inside and outside the ring (two trenches).

substrate.note: BOX thickness not stated.

tuning_nm_per_v.note: Red shift toward negative bias, so blue shift per positive volt: negative sign; magnitude 24.5 pm/V (0 to -4 V average)

devices.notes: Version: all values from arXiv 2509.01555v1 (55 pp incl. Supplementary Information), not the Laser & Photonics Reviews version of record. One physical device (8 um radius ring, 40 um doped region); two rows split by operating point (0 V self-biasing here, -3 V depletion in hu2026-b). Static spectral values (Q, FSR, ER, IL, tuning, Vpi*L) sit on this row only. Fig. 3(d) EO S21 curves are normalized; reference frequency of the 3 dB drop not stated. 3 dB BW at 0 V is operating-point dependent (83, 97, more than 110 GHz at 6, 5, 4 dB IL, optical peaking); wafer map (9 dies, 6 dB point, Fig. 3(e)) reads 81.8 to 93.6 GHz at 0 V (text says above 82 GHz; centre die 83.6). Vpi*L is a resonance-shift-derived figure (0 to -4 V average), not a phase-shifter Vpi. Junction Rs about 31 ohm at 0 V (simulated, p.39). Heater 81.2 pm/mW. Temperature: normalized OMA of a 64 GBd NRZ eye over a 1.5 K range (p.45, Fig. S6). Optical power at the 32 Gb/s demo: Rop 3 dBm for BER below 1e-12 (p.15); PCIe 5.0 eye width meets 9.375 ps. Not reported: Vpi at a single bias, RF Vpi, doping levels, BOX thickness, cladding, fabricator name (12-inch CMOS foundry), on-chip optical power for data runs, temperature class, BER values for the PAM4 and 180 GBd eyes. drive_vpp_v is the authors' estimated swing at the DUT (cable attenuation factor, Fig. S10), not an on-chip measurement.

Co-packaged transmitter: 150 um Si photonic-crystal-waveguide MZM (design same as the authors' earlier Optica 2024 paper) plus the driver. Row -a is the nominal ng = 35 +/- 5 spectral point near 1537 nm; wavelength is the reference wavelength stated for the ng spread, the laser wavelength of the data runs is not stated. 3 dB bandwidth 50 GHz is the tunable-peaking-ON label for ng = 35 in Fig. 4(c) (peaking OFF: 42 GHz); the EO sweep covered 1 to 40 GHz at PDC 260 mW with the whole transmitter (driver, bond wires), and the labelled crossing sits on the co-simulated curve beyond the measured range, so bw_measured_to is 40 and the basis is simulated (a crossing read on the co-simulation curve beyond the measured range). The 50 GHz bandwidth is at PDC = 260 mW with peaking ON for the whole transmitter; it is not the bandwidth of the 50 mW / 0.78 pJ/bit operating point, whose bandwidth is not reported (ER 1.4 dB and energy are at 50 mW). Row mixes these two operating points; no separate row is split out. Energy 0.78 pJ/bit = 50 mW / 64 Gb/s with a 5-tap receiver FFE (SD-FEC compatible); DSP-free best 1.0 pJ/bit (50 Gb/s, 50 mW); with laser (80 mW at assumed 20% WPE) and bias control (3.3 mW) the total rises to 133 mW and 2.1 pJ/bit. Extinction ratio 1.4 dB is that of the unprocessed 64 Gb/s eye at 50 mW (4.0 dB at 260 mW). Active footprint 0.66 mm^2 (modulator 0.3 mm^2); on-chip insertion loss about 11 dB including about 8 dB from the PN-doped PCW phase shifter; PCW 3 dB operating bandwidth 5.9 nm; 2.6 nm spectral shift from 0 to 300 mW (25 to 84 C simulated); quadrature bias heater at most 3.3 mW. Z0 about 50 ohm is the simulated electrode impedance (LH raises it from 30 ohm). Laser 13 dBm is the tunable-laser output (coupling loss not stated); the source amplitude to the driver was 0.4 Vpp (not the modulator swing). Not reported: Vpi, modulator-level drive swing, electrode dimensions, doping, junction capacitance, temperature class. bw3db_reference 1ghz is derived: Fig. 4(c) is normalized and the sweep starts at 1 GHz, but the normalization frequency is not stated.

devices.notes: Racetrack resonator (critically coupled, FSR 0.781 nm) modulated at the 3 dB transmission point (detuned to f_res + kappa/2); push-push operation because the 8 um acoustic wavelength divides the 400 um arm separation (p.26-27). VpiL is a resonance-shift-derived value (convention q): no Vpi in volts is stated and none is derived; length_mm 0.4 = two 200 um straight sections of one racetrack, both acoustically driven (push-push), the length used for the VpiL (Table S1 Lc). Drive: 0.235 V peak is a value the authors compute from the S11 power delivered to the IDT, not a probe measurement; 504 MHz is below 1 GHz so the VpiL is a quasi-static (dc) entry per convention m. Mechanism split from simulation (p.7): photoelastic > 90 %, moving boundary and secondary Pockels small. Optical resonator: intrinsic Q = 70k +- 1.3k (Fig. 3d label Qi, intrinsic, so q_loaded left empty), linewidth kappa/2pi = 5.63 +- 0.07 GHz (p.7), non-resolved-sideband regime (504 MHz < kappa). Optical input: -19 dBm at the photoreceiver, peak S21 -30.5 dB (p.9); no on-chip launch power stated, so optical_input_power_dbm is empty. Temperature: cryostat 5 K (temperature_k approx: device 5.46 K at 0 dBm, not stated at 1 dBm, Fig. S8a); the optical resonance shows a thermal blue shift with RF power (6.26 K rise at 10 dBm, Fig. S8). The IDT S11 is at 0 dBm with a 3 V/um bias in Fig. 1; the VpiL measurement used 1 dBm and no stated DC bias. Modulation depth 2.2 dB peak-to-peak at 504 MHz is labelled ER in Fig. 3e; stated as dynamic.

devices.notes: Single device: MZM with one plasmonic BTO phase shifter in each arm (200 um arm-length asymmetry), SiN from a foundry-produced platform (foundry not named), BTO wafer-scale integrated after planarization, BEOL plasmonic section. Vpi columns: MZM-level numbers whose arm drive is not stated (Fig. 1a shows two phase shifters; push-pull not stated); Vpi,DC 3.2 V and VpiL 0.048 V mm are taken from the fringe/resonance shift of the unbalanced MZI (200 um arm-length asymmetry), hence vpi_convention resonance_tuning_derived; the RF Vpi 9.6 V is a different method (sideband ratio, Eq. 3, p.5); high-frequency Vpi 9.6 V (0.144 V mm) is larger than at DC, attributed to BTO dispersion between low and high frequency; the abstract "VpiL 144 V um" is the RF value. Reference phase shifter of the same cross section and length shows a 5-6 dB drop between MHz and low GHz (Fig. 5a); the MZM response was measured only 10-70 GHz, so the bandwidth is referenced to the 10 GHz start, normalization otherwise not stated. Optimum DC bias about +/-2.5 V after +/-5 V (Fig. 6, hysteresis); 3 V DC poling bias in data runs; bias for Vpi not stated. Optical input 18 dBm EDFA output into the SiN chip (before grating couplers, not entered); 3.5 dB grating couplers. BER 3.98e-2 (216 GBd 2PAM) and 3.89e-2 (128 GBd 4PAM): the paper says below the SD-FEC limit (SD-FEC with 20% overhead, p.6); the BER threshold value is not printed. Simplified DSP (single 151-tap linear equalizer) stays below the SD-FEC limit up to 160 GBd (Fig. 8). Not reported: ER, net rate, energy per bit, capacitance, temperature, electrode thickness, substrate. Inventory title mismatch: the batch hint title ("200 Gbit/s Barium Titanate Modulator Using Weakly Guided Plasmonic Modes") is a different title; the Crossref title and the paper text agree.

Per-cavity fit (Table I p.4, fitted to Fig. 3b,c and 4b): Q 6.6e4 / 7.4e4, total linewidth 2.9 / 2.6 GHz (cavity 1 / 2), kappa_c/kappa_i 0.46 / 1.42, tuning 1.15 / 1.09 GHz/V; first-order perturbation theory gives 1.0 GHz/V (p.3, Supp VI). Row tuning 0.0092 nm/V is the cavity-1 slope read from Fig. 3b (cavity 2: 8.7 pm/V, Fig. 3c); q_loaded 70000 is the paper approximate value (text p.2). 3 dB cutoff around 1.5 GHz for each cavity (Fig. 4a, small-signal, plotted 0 to 5 GHz, matches the fitted linewidths); reference entered as dc (curve normalised at 0 GHz, not stated by the authors). ER: more than 30 dB at the two destructive-interference minima of |t_IQ|^2 (Fig. 4b inset, p.3), static. 4-QAM drive: +-1 V on each cavity (2 V peak to peak, p.2; p.3); no baud rate stated (the modulation frequency 1 GHz is not identified as a symbol rate), so max_baud and line rate left empty. Energy 25.8 fJ/bit = 51.5 fJ/symbol / 2 bits from a COMSOL Maxwell capacitance matrix (C11 10.6, C12 9.4, C22 22.2 fF) and a 0D circuit simulation with 0-2 V swing (Supp VI p.19), an author estimate. Geometry: 600 nm film, 400 nm etch (slab 200 nm derived), 35 deg outer sidewall and about 17 deg inner sidewall in the Bragg gaps (p.6), waveguide 800 nm tapering to 900 nm in the PhC, Bragg period 426 nm, 660 nm directional-coupler gap, 12:88 measured splitting ratio at 1548.65 nm (Supp Fig. 3, p.14). Electrode gap not stated in text. Facet insertion loss 8.2 dB (15 percent transmission, faulty facet etch; about 3 dB in other runs) in Supp IX p.26 is not entered because the paper does not define it as on-chip or fiber-to-fiber loss. Fabrication yield 64 percent: 18 of 28 resonant two-sided cavities (of 51 measured) with Q above 2e4 (Supp Fig. 11, p.18). Coherent receiver (AIM Photonics silicon PIC) limited detection to 2 GHz. Sidewall angle 35 deg is measured from the chip normal as stated on p.6 (55 deg from the film plane); other rows in the atlas may use the film plane. Fig. 4a draws both -3 dB and -6 dB reference lines and the paper does not state whether dB is optical or electrical power; the 1.5 GHz matches the -3 dB line and the fitted linewidths.

BTO MZMs "integrated into the commercial 8-inch SiPh process" (foundry_native, fab not named), measured as stand-alone devices; waveguide material, electrode type, GS probe geometry not given. HSPS "single-ended drive scheme enabling standard push-pull driving with a Vpi of 3.6 V"; the 3.6 V is the MZM-level Vpi under push-pull drive (vpi_convention mzm_push_pull, derived from this sentence). Row mixes drive amplitudes: drive_vpp_v and energy are the 0.83 Vpp driver-less point of Table II (BER 3.5e-3); the 300 Gb/s PCS-PAM-8 point used a 3.7 Vpp drive (conclusion, p.7), PAM-4 and PAM-6 at 112 GBd the optimum 3.3 Vpp (eltes2023 gives 3 Vpp for the same points) and 100 GBd PAM-8 3.7 Vpp (p.4). Driver-less swings: 600 mVpp for OOK and 800 mVpp for PAM-4 (p.6) versus 830 mVpp maximum. 6 dB bandwidth of the C-band modulators within 40-50 GHz (range across samples, lower end entered as a bound); Fig. 2b/c spectra show a 5 dB response drop at 40 GHz (signal-spectrum derived, not entered). Optical input: ECL 15 dBm laser output, not power at the chip; grating couplers about 5 dB each; 500 m SSMF. Abstract states IL about 2 dB, static tuning about 100 uW. DC tuner power below 100 uW. Not reported: RF loss, n_RF, geometry.

D33), not a read-out DC half-wave; push-pull convention is the authors' label and was not independently confirmed; delta n_eff 6.97e-7 per V extracted vs 1.279e-6 simulated for the racetrack. The 0.4 dB is an excess loss of the filter-plus-modulator path read from Fig. 4(b), not a defined insertion loss; normalization of Fig. 4(b) not stated; grating-coupler exclusion is inferred from Fig. 4(a) only.

devices.notes: Same physical 7 mm device as liu2025-b, measured at 1550 nm. Fig. 8(a) transmission sweep at 1 MHz; drive and push-pull are not stated by the authors (GSG layout with an arm in each gap, Fig. 1(b)). Measured 3 dB bandwidth is a bound (far beyond 110 GHz; Table II '> 110'), entered as 110 gt; the authors' analytical-model extrapolation 220 GHz (matches measurement to 110 GHz) is a prediction, not a column; simulated design value about 240 GHz. Roll-off 0.77 dB up to 110 GHz is worded 'only' and 'less than'. Electrical S21 loss is about 3.4 dB up to 110 GHz for 7 mm (Fig. 7(a)); 35 ohm on-chip termination; RF line parameters here apply to both rows. Energy 4.42 fJ/bit uses Vrms 245.6 mV for 390 Gbit/s PAM8 and includes probe and cable. Eye diagrams only (Fig. 9), no BER stated. Fig. 9 labels PAM8 at 112 Gbaud as 112 Gbit/s, likely a typo. Fig. 8(b),(c): measured 1550 nm trace is noisy, about -0.4 to -1.2 dB over 104-110 GHz (approx. reading).

devices.notes: IL scope is uncertain (audit F4, 2026-10-03): abstract and conclusion give 5.7 dB (at -7 V), p.3 gives 6.3 dB and 'on-chip IL = 14.6 dB' for the same device, and the authors never say what each excludes; il_onchip_db holds the headline 5.7 dB, not the 14.6 dB the paper itself labels on-chip. Numbers from arXiv v2 (2412.19306v2, 6 pages); no DOI or journal version found. Mechanism: ITO free-carrier accumulation/depletion in an Al/Al2O3/ITO capacitor (plasmonic enhancement, TM mode), not Pockels; eo_material other (ITO has no enum value). IL: abstract and conclusion give 5.7 dB (at -7 V); p.3 says 6.3 dB 'on-chip IL = 14.6 dB' for the same device (14.6 dB matches the 9.3 um point of the cutback fit y = -0.64x - 8.51, Fig. 3(b), so it likely includes fiber facets and passive waveguide); 5.7 dB entered. Facet coupling 3.5 dB per facet; junction loss 0.6 dB measured (simulation 2.2 dB per junction); passive Si3N4 TM waveguide loss 1.29 dB/cm. Static ER 1.5 dB at +/-12 V and 0.85 dB at +/-7 V (Fig. 3(c)); 3D simulation gives 3.7 and 1.9 dB. Final ITO carrier concentration 3.0e20 cm-3 (1.9e20 after lift-off). Capacitance 400 fF measured (162 fF calculated), resistance 1140 Ohm measured (717 Ohm calculated); simulated electrical 3 dB bandwidth 1.36 GHz. S21 fit: 3 dB at 1.05 GHz and 6 dB at 2.3 GHz (Fig. 4(d), normalized S21, reference level not stated); fit-defined, so bw_basis derived (audit R2-F1). One-port and two-port RF electrodes fabricated; the one-port version is shown. Optimized-geometry bandwidth beyond 260 GHz is an expectation citing Ref. [7], not entered. Wavelength 1550 nm, TM polarization. Metal stack Ti/Al, thicknesses not stated.

devices.notes: Single device; numbers from the Nature Communications version of record, its Supplementary Information and the Author Correction (Fig. 1c label 4 mm -> 4 um; no value changes). Vpi 1.8 V comes from Table 1 and equals the measured Vpi*L of 1.44 V cm at 1.55 um over the 8 mm arm; frequency, wavelength sweep and drive convention of the Vpi measurement are not stated (text calls Vpi a static parameter), so vpi_convention and drive stay unspecified. The two 8 mm arms are 200 um apart (p.3); two gold strip lines (Fig. 1b) are fed by a single G-S-G probe (Fig. 1d); how the arms are driven is not stated. Two source statements bear on the drive form but neither names it: Methods p.7 (Energy consumption) says "with dual-drive configuration, the energy consumption could be further reduced", implying the measured device was not dual-drive; Supplementary Note 2 (p.3-4) defines the half-wave voltage as the voltage producing a phase shift of pi and Eq. 5.b uses a single phase-shifter length L with no push-pull factor of 2, so the 1021 pm/V extraction (r33 223 pm/V) assumes the full pi over one 8 mm length. With the single G-S-G feed and vertical poling against a common bottom electrode this points to single-arm operation, but the authors do not state it; drive and vpi_convention stay unspecified. Bandwidth: measured 3 dB EO bandwidth around 68 GHz read on a VNA limited to 70 GHz (Fig. 1f; fitted line, ripple up to about +1 dB above the 0 dB start); normalisation frequency not stated (low_freq_unstated); the 6 dB bandwidth is only presumed over 70 GHz and is not entered. Loss (Supplementary Note 5): fiber-to-fiber loss about 10 dB = about 3 dB per facet lensed-fibre edge coupling x 2, Y-junctions about 1.4 dB, and about 2.6 dB on-chip waveguide/phase-shifter loss, which with a 12 mm total device length gives the 0.22 dB/mm (2.2 dB/cm) propagation loss, also stated as confirmed on a straight reference waveguide (not shown). Main text gives no insertion loss. Electrode: gold strip line 16 um wide, 3 um thick over a bottom aluminium electrode, G-S-G probe pads (Fig. 1d); Z0 is a design target matched to 50 ohm (Supplementary Note 3, CST FEM, close to 50 ohm over 20-200 GHz, no value) not a measured impedance; electrode_type other because no enum fits; n_RF not reported (text says refractive indices of microwave and light are comparable). In-device n^3 r33 = 1021 pm/V at 1.55 um; Supplementary Note 2 / Table 1 give in-device r33 = 223 pm/V with n = 1.66 (derived by the authors from Vpi*L = 1.44 V cm, confinement 0.738, d_eo 1 um, d_c 6 um, eps about 3; the main text quotes polymer index 1.67 from the modal calculation), Tg 172 C, poling 300-400 V near Tg. Cryogenic dc electro-optic tuning efficiency near the working bias Vbias = -100 V: d(omega_a)/dV = 2pi x 145 MHz/V (p.26, Fig. 22, linear fit; measurement temperature not stated, so temperature_k is empty). Sign contradiction: the text gives 2pi x 145 MHz/V (positive implied, no sign printed) while the plotted fit slopes negative (optical detuning falls from about +2.5 GHz to about -2.3 GHz as Vbias goes from -100 V to -65 V); tuning_nm_per_v is therefore left empty under convention (y) and both readings are kept here (conversion at 1603.5 nm would be 1.24 pm/V in magnitude); Fig. 2(i) (75 mK, p.5) shows the same sign as Fig. 22 (resonance frequency falls with increasing Vbias), and the Fig. 22 slope magnitude, about 140 MHz/V, agrees with 145 MHz/V. Post-cooldown room-temperature tuning efficiency about 2pi x 395 MHz/V versus the tuning voltage Vtune (dc-tuning port, not Vbias), 0 to -100 V, with inverted polarity (p.26, Fig. 23; not a separate row). Effective r = 13 pm/V is more than an order of magnitude below the 200 pm/V cited from earlier BaTiO3 films (p.7). g0/2pi = 406 Hz (Appendix E2, Table V). devices.notes: VERSION arXiv v1. Folded layout with waveguide crossing: two 5.5 mm interaction sections (11 mm total), physical length 7.8 mm; output 2x2 MMI gives two complementary outputs. Vpi 2.98 V from a 150 kHz triangular sweep (Fig. 7(f)); abstract says less than 3.0 V; Vpi*L 3.3 V cm is the abstract value (2.98 V x 11 mm = 3.28). EO response measured as optical sidebands 3-40 GHz at 1550 nm with UV15 present (Fig. 11); text: roll-off about 0.1 dB/GHz, 3 dB bandwidth roughly 30 GHz (3 dB divided by the rounded 0.1 dB/GHz slope, entered as derived); low frequencies omitted because of unlevel RF source, so the reference frequency is not defined. Fig. 11 fitted slopes 0.108-0.137 dB/GHz. RF index: UV15-clad about 2.10, air-clad about 1.85 (p.5, Fig. 5(c); these are the values near 40 GHz, UV15 falls from about 2.4 at 1 GHz to about 2.13 at 20 GHz, air-clad from about 2.1 to 1.89 at 10 GHz); optical group index about 2.14 (simulated); electrode impedance 43-53 ohm over 5-40 GHz in Fig. 5(d), not entered (one-line curve). Text says electrode S21 at 40 GHz is roughly -3 dB (air) and -4 dB (UV15), but Fig. 5(a),(b) show S(1,2) about -5.8 dB (air) and -7.2 dB (UV15) at 40 GHz (text and figure disagree); electrode length not stated. ER 45 dB: OSA peak-to-null in Fig. 8 gives 45.5 dB (port 1) and 45.4 dB (port 2); power meter reads higher, the lower OSA value used; reverse operation about 33 dB. Fiber-to-fiber loss 12.0 dB = 2 x 4.44 dB coupling + 1.1 dB path + 2.02 dB alignment (author accounting). Ground width 75 um. Thermo-optic bias P_pi 92 mW. Fabricator not named.

devices.notes: Vpi measured at 1 MHz with a triangle waveform (Methods p.5). Push-pull GSG CPW electrodes stated (p.2). Electrode signal and ground widths and whether the Au contacts the LN slab or sits on cladding are not stated. Wavelength series on one 1 cm, 3 um gap device (Fig. 2(a)); text value. Headline device. 3 dB EO bandwidth about 35 GHz with respect to 3 GHz (Bessel-fit of sideband power, Fig. 2(c)); abstract says in excess of 35 GHz; theory 36 GHz from measured CPW S-parameters; limited by RF loss. Plotted data run to about 40 GHz. Insertion loss: on-chip loss about 0.7 +- 0.2 dB/cm from varied-length 3 um gap devices (supplementary, wavelength not stated in main text); total about 15 dB fiber-to-fiber includes about 7 dB/facet lensed-fiber coupling (wavelength and exact definition not stated). ER about 21 dB (Fig. 2(b) inset, 1 cm, 3 um gap, static transmission sweep). RF loss: only the fitted coefficient 1.35 dB/cm/GHz^0.5 is stated (p.3); no point value entered. RF index 2.22 at 50 GHz and optical group index about 2.38 (VNIR) are simulated; Electrodes designed for Z close to 50 ohm (COMSOL, p.2); authors cite a CPW impedance mismatch for the low-frequency roll-off (p.3); fabricated Z0 not reported. Index mismatch about 0.17. MZM is an unbalanced amplitude modulator with Y-splitters (0.2 dB excess loss each). Discussion (p.5) 'on-chip insertion loss as low as 0.7 dB' restates 0.7 dB/cm over 1 cm; il_onchip_db left empty (Y-splitters about 0.2 dB each, p.2). Mixed source (convention z): Vpi at 738 nm is from the Fig. 2(a) wavelength series of one 1 cm MZM; the paper does not state that the bandwidth, ER and loss come from the same device.

devices.notes: VERSION: version of record (Laser Photonics Rev. 19, 2401092) with the Supporting Information (docx text, cited by section). Rows a-e are wavelength operating points of one 1 mm push-pull slow-light MZM (physical device shared with shen2025-sys; shen2025-design is the simulation of the same design). Row a = 1547.1 nm, the best point. Vpi 2.1 V from a 10 kHz triangular sweep (Table 1: 2.1 V @10 kHz); the paper warns that near-DC sweeps can over- or under-estimate Vpi because of the photorefractive effect (p.4). EO S21 (Fig. 3(b), 110 GHz LCA) shows no -3 dB crossing up to 110 GHz, so 110 is a bound equal to the measurement limit; the plotted trace is normalised and rises to about +4 dB; Table 1 lists the roll-off as 0 dB at 110 GHz (not entered). Simulated 3 dB bandwidth 235 GHz is on row shen2025-design. Static ER 27.5 dB here; minimum ER over the slow-light range is 12.7 dB at 1546 nm (supplement Section 12, Fig. S14). Dynamic eye ER 3.3, 2.1, 1.5 dB at 120, 150, 180 Gbps NRZ (Fig. 4(b-d)); these are on shen2025-sys. Optical loss: the supplement calls the on-chip loss wavelength dependent, 5.8 dB minimum and 16.9 dB maximum over 1544.9-1547.1 nm, mean 9.3 dB (supplement Section 7, Fig. S9); the paper does not say whether the grating couplers are included, so il_onchip_db 12.4 dB is entered with scope undefined, read from Fig. S9 (supplement docx image, transmission vs wavelength, 1544.9-1547.1 nm), about +/-0.3 dB (trace end at 1547.1 nm). The readings at the other wavelengths are about 10.2 dB (1546.92 nm, b) and about 15.3 dB (1546.7 nm, c), each about +/-1 dB on a steep slope, and about 13.0 dB (1546.1 nm, d); b and c are in notes only; 1535 nm (e) is outside the plotted range. Not reported: signal/ground widths, SiN waveguide width, arm spacing, cladding, temperature, optical power. Supplement figures are embedded in source.docx (word/media); Fig. S9, S12 and S14 are raster images and were read; Fig. S8 and S11 are EMF and were not rendered. Fig. S9 was read from the supplement docx image word/media/image36.jpeg (transmission vs wavelength).

devices.notes: Version: arXiv 2210.06994v1 (9 pp, IEEE template placeholder header), no journal DOI located. Ring-assisted MZM (racetrack phase shifter on one arm of a symmetric MZI), measured at Vbias = 1 V reverse (paper quotes the magnitude; negative sign here follows the repo reverse-bias convention). SFDR 75 dB Hz^(2/3) (Fig. 9(a), carrier-injection-like nonlinearity). Vpi*L 0.70 V cm is the low end of the stated range. Bandwidth is measured with a 17.5 GHz photodetector; the response shows optical peaking and is normalized at the lowest frequency (about 1 GHz), reference unspecified. Static ER 21.5 dB and FSR 7.7 nm are measured at Vbias = 0 V (Fig. 4(a)) and are carried on the 1 V row only. Racetrack straight 2.25 um, gap 0.2 um, power coupling 0.77 (simulated, overcoupled by design); MZI arm 375 um (not the phase-shifter length); PN junction covers 44 percent of the 180-degree bends; 99 percent of the mode lies in the P/N regions (overlap analysis). Vpi*L definition and active length are not stated, so no length or Vpi is entered. Fabricator not named (platform said to be commercially available; one author is at CompoundTek). Not reported: insertion loss, Vpi in volts, active length, energy, optical power, wavelength tolerance. No 0 V row exists: the static ER 21.5 dB and FSR 7.7 nm are Vbias = 0 V values although bias_for_vpi_v here is -1 V.

devices.notes: VPI CONTRADICTION kept visible (audit F1, 2026-10-03): the abstract (p.1) says measurement results indicate VpiL below 1.2 V.mm 'are possible' for balanced MZMs with this slot, but the only measurement of this 1 mm device, Fig. 11 (p.12), is a spectral shift of about 120 pm for 1 V with FSR about 1.15 nm. That gives Vpi = FSR / (2 x 0.12 nm/V) = 4.8 V, i.e. VpiL = 4.8 V.mm (0.48 V.cm), a factor of 4.0 above the abstract bound; reading the two nulls in the Fig. 11 render gives a spacing of about 1.3 nm (marker labelled 1.15 nm), which would give about 5.4 V.mm. The body states no measured Vpi, drive or convention and the authors do not reconcile the two, so vpil_dc_vcm, vpi_basis and vpi_convention are left empty instead of entering either number. Measured spectral shift 120 pm for 1 V with FSR about 1.15 nm (Fig. 11, p.12). Peak poling current 206 nA with TiO2, below one third of the untreated slot (Fig. 10(b), p.11-12); poling at 100 V/um minimum, 80 to 150 C ramp, Tg about 145 C. Coupling loss is reported separately for the PIC (average about 12 dB per photonic-wire-bond channel, about 10.5 dB per grating coupler, p.7); the definition of the 0.78 dB is not stated. Two phase-shift mechanisms: slow birefringence response (f-6dB 119 kHz, strong) and fast Pockels response (f-6dB 7.8 GHz, about 30 dB weaker in S21); DC tuning 150 pm/V (abstract, text, Fig. 3(e)) vs 250 pm/V (Fig. 3(c) caption). Fig. 3(c) graphic also annotates about 0.65 dB off-resonance loss and FWHM about 150 pm at 1534.5 nm (Q about 10k by arithmetic), versus 0.78 dB and Q 15340 in caption and abstract; the paper is internally inconsistent on IL, FWHM/Q and tuning efficiency, and the caption/abstract values are entered. Fig. 6 caption lists 'experimentally obtained' eta_ps 0.69e-5 /V, Vpp 368 V and f-3dB 2.1 GHz that are not consistent with the main text; not used. 3 dB bandwidth not reported. Footprint about 0.084 mm2 (8400 um2). Fabricated at Advanced Micro Foundry (DUV, SOI); FN-LC (pm-158, Polaris Electro-Optics) hand-coated post-foundry; no passivation step in the PIC demo. electrode_gap_um = d1, metal electrode to waveguide core distance (Fig. 2(a), p.8); counter-contact is through the doped Si slab. devices.notes: Numbers from arXiv v1 (2506.03281v1, 21 pages, 3 Jun 2025); no DOI or journal version found. Static optical transmission measured on grating-coupler test structures (about 6 dB per coupler, extracted from reference waveguides; p.11) with 1 mW laser input; IL is relative to the device loss before fabrication. Graphene mobility about 8000 cm2/Vs, Au/SLG contact resistance 215 to 995 Ohm um (p.11). Fabricating fab not named in the text; the 200 mm SOI process is cited to Ref. [103] (Littlejohns et al., Appl. Sci. 10, 2020, with a CORNERSTONE URL), so foundry_or_fab is left empty. Headline device: f3dB 67 GHz (S21, 40 nm gate dielectric), NRZ up to 80 Gbit/s. f3dB is extrapolated from -55.5 to -58.5 dB on an upper-envelope fit of S21 (p.15), so bw_basis is derived (authors' extrapolation of a fit) with an approx qualifier; the reference level is the low-frequency plateau at about -55.5 dB, not DC. Approximate reading of Fig. 9(b) (log axis, p.14): the envelope fit meets the -58.5 dB line near 66 GHz and the trace ends near 67 GHz, which is also the probe and bias-tee rating, so the value rests on the fit at the end of the measured range and no data point is clearly beyond it. Dynamic ER about 1.2 dB at 80 Gbit/s with Vpp about 7 V (Table IV; modulation efficiency about 0.01 dB/V/um between 10.5 and 13 V). Table I active area 40 x 0.55 um (about 22 um2). Table IV (CTLE-filtered): BER 1.2e-7 at 50, 2.9e-5 at 60, 8.5e-3 at 80 Gbit/s for 40 um; 80 um and 100 um devices (gate dielectric not stated) also shown at 80 Gbit/s with BER 1.9e-2 and 1e-2. Static ER slope 0.09 dB/um (Fig. 8(d)). Simulated EO-BW for 40 um in the 40 nm design is about 70 GHz (Fig. 2(e)). Energy per bit is the authors' CVpp^2/4 figure; C and Vpp behind it are not stated. Energy check (reader arithmetic, approximate): 58 fJ/bit = C Vpp^2/4 with the 7 V of the eye measurement would need C about 4.7 fF, whereas eps0 eps_r A/d with eps_r 6.8, d 40 nm and A about 22 um2 gives about 33 fF, which would correspond to Vpp near 2.7 V; the authors give neither C nor V for the 58 fJ/bit, so the cell is unchanged. Gate dielectric: Methods (p.9) give 3.5 nm hBN plus 40 nm PE-ALD Al2O3, while the Fig. 2 caption and Table I call 40 nm the gate oxide; the 40 nm label may be the Al2O3 only or the total. Fig. 9(b) is absolute S21 referenced to the stated -55.5 dB plateau; low_freq_unstated is the closest reference value.

devices.notes: Quasi-static ferroelectric operation: Vpi*L is the author-computed value for the effective Pockels coefficient r_eff 345 +/- 30 pm/V (4 K, remanent zero-field point after poling; r_eff 140 +/- 30 pm/V at 1.6 V/um) and depends on bias history; only the lower MZI arm is modulated (Fig. 3b), 20 Hz, 16 V amplitude over the 10 um gap. A phase shift of pi corresponds to a field change of 0.084 V/um (p.6); VpiL quoted as 1.04 +/- 0.08 V cm; no Vpi in volts is stated and none is derived here. VpiL 1.04 uses meander-corrected r_eff 345 pm/V (280 pm/V measured / 0.81, Supplement Eq. 20-22); measured device: 0.084 V/um x 10 um x 1.537 cm = about 1.29 V cm. Bandwidth: response flat from about 20 Hz to 1 MHz by an indirect time-averaged power method (response drops below about 20 Hz, attributed to DC screening); setup resonance near 5 MHz; no 3 dB crossing observed, so 1 MHz = 0.001 GHz is a bound and the measurement limit (convention (c)); it is not a measured 3 dB bandwidth and is tagged bw_indirect_method. Electrode type 'lumped' and single-ended drive are inferred from the quasi-static wire-bonded drive and the Fig. 3b caption (authors do not name the electrode type). Waveguide platform 'other' (PMMA-loaded SrTiO3 on SiO2/Si); integration 'other' (MBE on Si, wafer bonded, Si removed). Wavelength 'around 1470 nm' (Supplement 4.1); 1.84 +/- 0.04 group index at 4 K from the FSR (Supplement p.29, formula in paper). Waveguide propagation loss and insertion loss are not given for the cryogenic MZI (extinction ratio limited by asymmetric splitting, no number); room-temperature cut-back loss is in the papers.csv notes.

devices.notes: Single device characterized; the paper does not explicitly restate that the Sec. 4 data chip is the Fig. 2 chip (tag device_identity_unresolved), so system results sit on this row. Wavelength 1550 nm is nominal (Eq. S13; data run near 1550 nm); wavelength of the Vpi and EO-response measurements is not stated. Drive about 1 Vpp: reference plane (amplifier output vs device) not stated; do not rank across rows without a plane tag. BER: 64 GBd OOK below 1e-6 (no errors in about 1e6 symbols); 100 GBd OOK 4e-6; 64 GBd PAM4 5e-5; 100 GBd PAM4 9e-3 (electrical back-to-back 1.7e-3). Operating point set by wavelength via 80 um arm imbalance, DC bias fine-tuning; EO response corrected for photodiode, probes, cables. Vpi measured at low frequency; no RF Vpi. Fiber-to-fiber loss includes grating couplers (about 5 dB each) and about 3 dB other passive loss; no on-chip-only number stated. In-device r33 about 34 pm/V (authors, from Vpi*L). Measured BTO film: eps_r about 18, tan delta about 0.05 at 60 GHz; BTO dielectric loss 0.58 dB/mm at 50 GHz. Authors' predictions not entered: velocity-mismatch 3 dB bandwidth about 220 GHz (derived), 1 um gold line bandwidth far beyond 100 GHz (simulated). Theory (linear model) predicts about 156 GHz. Optical power: 110 mW (20.4 dBm) is the maximum on-chip peak power tested in the feeder waveguide, no EO degradation; edge couplers (not the MZM) were damaged above 150 mW. IL measured at 1 mW low power. ER is the mean of the unmodulated asymmetric-MZI fringes over 50 nm (max 31 dB at 1560 nm), FSR 2.3 nm. Propagation loss 0.6 dB/cm (hybrid, cited from earlier work) and 0.8 dB/cm (transition) are in the text but not entered. Total chip 1.7 cm; hybrid region 1.4 cm; electrode 5 mm. Not reported: RF loss, ground electrode width, waveguide lateral position, bias, temperature. The Fig. 5(a) LCA trace (cyan) is a second, identically designed MZM on a different chip (p.8); S21 trace only, no separate row. No data modulation reported (small-signal EO S21 and Vpi only). devices.notes: Single intensity MZM; numbers from the ACS Photonics version of record and its Supporting Information. Vpi 1.7 V from Fig. 3(c) (100 kHz triangular drive; wavelength not stated, the paper says C-band); VpiL 2.13 V cm is the authors' 1.7 V x 12.5 mm; the simulated VpiL 2.4 V cm (58.2 percent LN confinement, push-pull) is not entered. drive push_pull and vpi_convention mzm_push_pull follow the supplement p.3 statement that the VpiL derivation assumes the push-pull configuration of the device; the measurement text does not name it. Bandwidth: bw3db_ghz 67 with gt is the end of the measured EO S21 trace (Fig. 4(e), p.4): the trace stays above about -2.4 dB up to its end near 67 GHz (about -2.3 dB there), so only 'more than 67 GHz' is shown by the data; bw_measured_to_ghz 67 (both extracted_from_figure). The paper claims '>70 GHz' (abstract, p.2, p.4, Table 1, conclusions) beyond the plotted measurement; that claim is not entered as a value. The EE S21 (6.4 dB point) 'surpasses 67 GHz' (Fig. 4(a)); the trace also ends at 67 GHz. The simulated 3 dB point of 100 GHz (p.4, model with the measured electrode parameters, green curve in Fig. 4(e)) is not entered. EO response normalisation frequency not stated. Loss: 2 dB insertion loss and 25 dB ER were measured before electrode deposition with the grating couplers normalised out (Fig. 3(b)); after full fabrication the chip loss is 10.2 dB including 7.2 dB for the two grating couplers, giving the 3 dB on-chip loss stated in the conclusion and Table 1 (10.2 - 7.2); the authors attribute the extra 1 dB to the metal electrodes. Hybrid-waveguide propagation loss is an author estimate (1.6 dB/cm, before electrodes). RF: fitted alpha0 0.49 dB/cm/GHz^0.5 (Fig. 4(d)) gives 4.01 dB/cm at 67 GHz (derived); n_rf about 2.6 is the plateau of Fig. 4(c) (design 2.5); the deduced Z0 ripples between about 48 and 55 ohm (Fig. 4(b)) so z0_ohm is empty; simulated Z0 50 ohm, n_rf 2.5 and alpha0 0.21 are not entered; ng 2.5 is the simulated optical group index marked in Fig. 2(d) and Fig. 4(c). CLTW dimensions (r,c,s,t,h,w,L) = (47,3,3,5,19,13,36) um (p.3), period r + c = 50 um (supplement p.3); T-structure thickness 200 nm. Data: dynamic ER better than 8 dB and drive voltages less than 2 V for all eyes (amplitude type not stated); eyes up to 168 Gbit/s; max_baud_gbd 100 is the 100 Gbit/s OOK line rate (derived). Not reported: measurement wavelength, optical input power, sidewall angle, Si substrate thickness, energy per bit, measured Z0. The lowest dip of the measured EO S21 trace is about -2.4 dB near 52 GHz.

The authors call it a push-pull MZM; they do not define the Vpi convention, so mzm_push_pull is an inference. EO bandwidth 'exceeding 67 GHz' is a text statement only; the paper shows no EO S21 and does not say how it was obtained (method unspecified); 67 GHz is the RF source limit (Anritsu 2-67 GHz; GSGSG probe rated 50 GHz, p.6), so bw_measured_to_ghz is empty. Extinction ratio left empty (convention y): text and annotation say carrier suppression 19.3 dB (Fig. 2c), but the plotted carriers of the maximum-point and null-point traces differ by about 9 dB (about -43 and -34 dBm), the arrow spans about 8 dB on the axis, and the legend (blue = maximum point, red = null point) conflicts with the caption (red = carrier-unsuppressed). electrode_type cl_twe from the cited design (p.3 'advanced slotted electrodes [56]', Kharel et al. micro-structured electrodes; cl_twe as for kharel2021) and the periodic loading features along the MZM gaps in Fig. 2(a); geometry not given. Not reported: electrode metal, gap, widths, rib width, cladding, optical loss, wavelength. Wafer stack from the commercial NanoLN LNOI specification in Methods (p.6); etch depth 'approximately 250 nm' leaving a 250 nm slab. System context: down-conversion 20-67 GHz, average conversion efficiency -44.1 dB, IF 20 GHz, SSR 37.2, 29.3, 26.1 dB, up-conversion to 110 GHz; the add-drop ring (FSR 196 GHz, 3 dB width about 3 GHz) and the double-pass phase modulator have no rows.

Drive 0.628 Vpp is stated at the sub-MZMs after cable and probe-array loss (RMS 161 mV). 1.96 Tb/s is the net rate with a 10 percent spatially-coupled LDPC FEC at 8.44 bit/symbol/pol; line rate not stated. 1.04 fJ/bit stated in the conclusion without formula or scope. CL-TWE dimensions (Fig. 1(b)): period 50 um, segment gap c 5 um, s 1 um, t 1 um, ws 80 um (the arrow spans the light region between the inner edges of the two segment rows in Fig. 1(b), not a stated signal-conductor width; not entered; by the 50 um scale bar the arm pitch is about 104 um). Electrode EE S21 roll-off 4.5 dB at 110 GHz and S11 below -15 dB (Fig. 4(d)); the authors use the 6.4 dB EE bandwidth as an estimate of the 3 dB EO bandwidth. Wavelength of Vpi and EO S21 measurements not stated: 1549.93 nm is the ECL line of the transmission experiment (simulation at 1550 nm). Total insertion loss about 18 dB with a lensed fiber, mainly mode mismatch; bending loss non-negligible. ER > 23 dB by DC measurement. Sidewall nearly 90 deg from horizontal with a ~20 deg slope at the bottom of one side (SEM, Fig. 4(b)). Waveguide width 1.3 um with an original mask width slightly larger to compensate lateral wet etching. Transmission: PAM-6 250 Gb/s BER 2.3e-2 and PAM-4 200 Gb/s BER 3.2e-3 (text), below both threshold lines of Fig. 6(b) (20 percent SD-FEC 2.4e-2 and HD-FEC 3.8e-3; the text cites only 2.4e-2); system limited by the 45 GHz AWG and 50 GHz amplifier; 100 Gbaud spectra and eyes in Fig. 6; baud of the 250 Gb/s point not stated. Laser output 17 dBm, signal after the modulator amplified to 1 dBm (EDFA). No supplement.

MATERIAL-ONLY, no device rows: bulk SrTiO3 (STO) crystals (5x5 mm chips, 0.5 or 1 mm thick), parallel-plate electrodes (30 nm Pt / 50 nm Au), free-space fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer at 1550 nm, 100 kHz drive (p.8 Methods); no waveguide or modulator device. PAPER-REPORTED MATERIAL NUMBERS (no column; all measured, bias-induced Pockels effect, T = 5 K or temperature of maximum with T < 10 K, 1550 nm, 100 kHz, Table I p.6): r33,max 580(60) / 840(50) / 1150(30) pm/V for natural STO / STO-28 (28% 18O) / STO-33 (33% 18O); d33,max 91(6) / 150(9) / 435(25) pC/N (authors give these as lower bounds, LN control read 4.6 vs known 6 pm/V, p.8-9); eps_r,max 26.0(1.5)k / 42.0(3.7)k / 82.0(1.6)k (LCR meter, 100 kHz, 1 V, p.8); field of max r33 0.080 / 0.036 / 0.008 MV/m; g11 0.15(2) / 0.21(3) / 0.30(1) m^4/C^2; q11 0.024(3) / 0.039(6) / 0.110(7) m^4/C^2; (P*eps_r)max 200(20) / 145(20) / 164(5) C/m^2; k33,max 0.15(1) / 0.21(2) / 0.46(3). Abstract: r33 exceeding 500 pm/V at 5 K (natural STO), above 1100 pm/V for STO-33. Fig. 4(a) p.6 gives the field dependence. Other: natural-STO low-frequency eps_r above 25,000 at low T (p.3, Fig. 2a); index 2.284 at 1550 nm (p.3); r13 = 170(20) pm/V, r33/r13 about 3.33 (Supplement S4, p.16); s11 at least 5e-15 m^2/V^2 (p.4). LN control r33 about 31 and r13 about 9 pm/V (p.8); bulk STO loss: intrinsic 0-0.2 dB/cm upper limit at room temperature, about 0.7 dB/cm saturated at low T, about 0.9 dB/cm peak near 75 V, below 0.55 dB/cm at 200 V (Supplement S8, p.18-19, Fig. S8); electro-optic bandwidth above 1 THz is a prediction from the Lyddane-Sachs-Teller relation (Supplement S6, p.18, predicted, not measured); measured RC cutoff about 1-4 MHz limited by sample capacitance (Supplement S5, p.17). Literature comparison values quoted in the text (LN r33 about 24 pm/V, BTO r42 about 170 pm/V at cryogenic T) are not this paper's measurements. No fabricator or wafer supplier named for the commercial STO chips. Stanford Nano Shared Facilities (now nano@stanford) appears as an author affiliation (NanoSIMS isotope check). papers.label: Chelladurai et al. 2025
papers.notes: VERSION: version of record, Nature Materials 24(6) 868-875, published online 2025-03-17, 11 pp; Supplementary Information (Notes 1-5, 23 pp, authors format unedited) is cached in references/chelladurai2025/supplement/ and was read (cited supplement p.N). License CC-BY-4.0 verified from Crossref (vor and tdm records, start 2025-03-17) and the rights statement on p.8; third-party material may carry other terms. MATERIAL-ONLY, no device rows: the 25 um BTO and 50 um LN phase shifters (5 um electrode separation, hybrid-gap-plasmon-style, p.2, p.9) are characterization vehicles; the main text reports no measured Vpi, bandwidth or loss for them (insertion loss about 0.2 dB is from mode simulation, p.2; simulated VpiL only described in Methods p.9, no values). PAPER-REPORTED MATERIAL NUMBERS (no column; optical 1550 nm; BTO films partially poled by DC bias then measured without bias, p.5 and p.9-10; sample temperature not stated; 100 MHz to 330 GHz; Pockels error bars are +/-2 standard errors of a fit over n = 15-20 devices, Fig. 4 caption): LN permittivity constant over the range, literature mean eps_a = 45 and eps_c = 27, confirmed by this work (p.3, Fig. 2c). BTO permittivity, Debye model with log-normal relaxation distribution (Eq. 2, Table 1 p.4, Fig. 2d p.3): this work (RF-sputtered 485 nm film) gamma0 = 72.6 +/- 2.3 GHz, sigma = 0.87 +/- 0.02, delta_eps = 905 +/- 26, eps_inf = 231 fixed from literature; literature fit gamma0 = 1.15 +/- 0.30 GHz, sigma = 0.92 +/- 0.20, delta_eps = 1862 +/- 149, eps_inf = 231 +/- 79; dispersion attributed to eps_a. LN Pockels, flat over 0.1-330 GHz: r33 = 26.9 pm/V and 1/2(r13 + 2 r42) = 15.0 pm/V (linear fits; text p.5, Fig. 4a p.6). BTO Pockels (Fig. 4b p.6): r33 = 125 pm/V at 100 MHz, Debye fit gamma0 = 565 MHz, sigma = 0.06, S_R = 75 pm/V, r_inf = 60 pm/V (flat about 60 pm/V above about 1 GHz; the Fig. 4 caption attributes these Debye parameters to the r42 data while the text on p.6 attributes them to r33; text followed); 1/2(r13 + 2 r42) = 481 pm/V at 100 MHz falling to 191 pm/V at 330 GHz via Miller's rule with delta = 0.327 +/- 0.002 pm/V and n0 = 2.26 at 1550 nm (p.6, Eq. 5). Literature clamped coefficients used for the r_eff(theta) curves, not measured here (p.10): BTO r33 = 30, r42 = 560, r13 = 6 pm/V; LN r33 = 31, r42 = 18, r13 = 9 pm/V. Max dn/dV order 1e-5 /V (LN) and 1e-4 /V (BTO) (Fig. 1 caption, p.2). Foundry entry from the acknowledgements (cleanroom team thanked); BTO film supplier from the acknowledgements. SUPPLEMENT ADDITIONS (re-check 2026-10-05; no main-text value changes): LN validation of the impedance model uses literature eps_c = 27, eps_a = 45 with no fitted parameters (supplement p.5, Fig. S1), LN devices of 50, 100, 150 um (Fig. S2); EO characterization uses the 50 um LN and 25 um BTO shifters, each GSG electrode carries two shifters with separate grating couplers (supplement p.7-8, Fig. S4). Pockels fits at 10 GHz (supplement p.16, Fig. S7): LN r13 + 2 r42 = 28.9 +/- 2.0 and r33 = 26.9 +/- 0.9 pm/V; BTO r13 + 2 r42 = 838 +/- 29 and r33 = 64.8 +/- 16.2 pm/V, with partially poled domain fractions 0.375 (0 and 90 deg) and 0.125 (180 and 270 deg); LN shifters at theta < 20 deg gave signals too weak to measure. Poling (supplement p.16-17, Fig. S8): DC bias raised in 1 V steps with a 50 GHz tone until the peak-sideband ratio saturated, bias removed, efficiency settles about 1 dB below the poled value; all measurements without bias because frequencies above 110 GHz precluded bias. Simulated VpiL in Fig. S10 and S11 (supplement p.20-21) are curves with constant r_eff = 440 pm/V (maximum of the fully poled case) or constant permittivity, no values stated in text; thickness uncertainty about 1 percent (BTO 485 nm film, error a few nm) and oxide error under 5 nm per 100 nm. Electrodes 200 nm (supplement p.12). Propagation loss about 20 dB/cm and 0.1 dB reflection give the approximately 0.2 dB insertion loss of a 50 um shifter (main p.2, simulation). Main text additions: 130 nm amorphous-Si grating couplers and 550 C O2 anneal for 1 h (p.9). The supplement adds no measured device-level Vpi, bandwidth or loss, so the paper stays material-only with no device rows. audit_status audited -> needs_audit because the row was re-distilled.

papers.notes: no_device_rows. VERSION: numbers come from the cached arXiv v1 preprint (2411.17070v1, 13 pp, no journal DOI located; no crossref.json). Identity: title and authors match the batch CSV (the CSV author list is truncated; 8 authors on the PDF title page, all CityU). Why no device rows: the paper is a single-sideband (SSB) generation scheme (mono-drive MZM with on-chip optical delay lines for a photonic 90 deg RF phase shift, FC-SSB and CS-SSB) and reports no Vpi, EO bandwidth, insertion loss, extinction ratio or data rate; its metrics (sideband suppression, sideband-to-carrier suppression, 3 dB SSB working bandwidth) have no device column and the 3 dB working bandwidth is that of the suppression ratio, not an EO bandwidth. Recorded here (p.6-10): FC-SSB max sideband suppression 22.1 dB at 50 GHz target (5 ps delay. Fig. 2(f) 21.1 dB and Fig. 2(g) 22.1 dB at the two quadrature points), 17.6 dB (lower) and 18.0 dB (upper) at the two quadrature points at 25 GHz (p.6, Fig. 2(c),(e)) and 20.6 dB at 27 GHz for the 25 GHz target (measured 3 dB suppression bandwidth 6.75 GHz centered at 27 GHz). CS-SSB at 25 GHz: sideband suppression 16.6 dB and sideband-to-carrier 16.8 dB (Fig. 4(b)); at 50 GHz (Fig. 4(f)): 22.5 dB sideband suppression and 16.9 dB sideband-to-carrier per the abstract and conclusion, while the p.10 body text swaps the two numbers; the Fig. 4(f) arrows (22.5 dB between the two sidebands, 16.9 dB carrier to selected sideband) look consistent with the abstract (figure read at page-render resolution). RF frequency shifting 50 GHz to 1 GHz with 1.0 kHz linewidth; over 30 dB improvement at about 26 GHz after 5 km SMF vs DSB. RF drive about 15 dBm (25 GHz) and 10 dBm (50 GHz). Supplement 1 (delay-line design, theory) not cached. Fabrication: Nanosystem Fabrication Facility (CWB) of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology acknowledged for device fabrication (acronym HKUST expanded). papers.label: Guo et al. 2026
papers.notes: VERSION: all numbers come from the cached arXiv v2 preprint (2603.14346v2, 16 pp, no date stamp, no journal DOI located; no crossref.json). Supplemental Notes 1-3 not cached. Identity: title and 12 authors match the batch CSV (the CSV list is truncated). Two rows: guo2026-a, the 3 mm push-pull CLTW MZM at 532 nm (headline, UWOC transmitter), and guo2026-b, the dual-drive MZM used for optical single-sideband and EO comb generation (no Vpi or bandwidth reported). repro_grade C and no sim config: substrate not stated, propagation direction not stated, and the CLTW parameters (g, r, c, s, t, h) = (3.5, 45, 5, 2, 2, 3.5) um are defined only by the unlabeled top-view schematic of Fig. 2(a) (the text does not define the letters and the sketch does not make clear which of g and h, both 3.5 um, is the electrode-to-waveguide gap vs the stem length), so the loaded and unloaded cross-sections cannot be built without guessing which letter is the electrode-to-waveguide gap; electrode_gap_um is therefore left empty. Judgment calls: Vpi 2.6 V (100 kHz sawtooth, Fig. 5(b)) and Vpi*L 0.78 V cm (the authors compute it from Vpi and the 3 mm length, so basis derived; simulated 0.77 V cm in notes) entered with approx because the paper writes about-equal; bandwidth ~50 GHz is a bound (gt): the intro says exceeds 50 GHz, the trace in Fig. 5(d) spans about 3 to 57 GHz with large ripple, touches -3 dB at about 33, 36, 48 and 56 GHz relative to a baseline near +1 dB, and the authors blame the visible photodiode; the 57 GHz end is read from the plot. ER entered as >35 dB static from the text and the Fig. 5(c) label; the Fig. 5(c) caption says ~32 dB (inconsistent). Fig. 5(c) peak about -21 dBm and null about -56 dBm. On-chip IL 2.7 dB is the authors subtraction of grating-coupler loss from about 12 dB fiber-to-fiber (12 minus 2 x 4.5 is 3.0, so the implied per-coupler loss is about 4.65 dB). Propagation loss 1.7 read from Fig. 4(b) for the 1.5 um width (y-axis labeled dB, text says dB/cm). RF values (loss about 5.5 dB/cm at 100 GHz, n_RF about 2.48, Z0 about 49 ohm, ng about 2.45) are simulated CLTW design values read at 100 GHz from Fig. 3 / text. Optical handling: stable for 1 h at 18 dBm input / >5 dBm output, quoted as about 11.5 dBm on-chip (the authors' own deduction, the paper shows no derivation, and the top of the tested range rather than a measured limit; basis author_estimate); a TFLN comparison device fluctuated above 10 dBm input. max_baud_gbd 100 is derived from 100 Gb/s OOK (1 bit per symbol); the PAM-4 point is 56 GBd, 112 Gb/s over 3 m; 64 Gb/s OOK over 9 m. BER threshold 3.8e-3; system limited by AWG/oscilloscope/photodiode, not the chip (authors). Not reported: substrate, wafer supplier, foundry (device fabricated in-house, facility not named), optical input power of the Vpi measurement, drive amplitude of the UWOC runs (SHF 807c saturates at about 6 Vpp), energy per bit. TO phase shifter 0.51 mm, P_pi about 50 mW. Batch CSV hints (flat to about 50 GHz, 112 Gb/s over 3 m, 64 Gb/s over 9 m) verified. Audit corrections 2026-10-03: see AUDIT_DISPOSITIONS.md.
